subject: The same 70-year-old woman's right knee wearing the strap, exactly as in the first frame: an extreme close-up, the kneecap and the strap filling the frame, the kneecap uncovered above the notch. The last frame is the same knee from further back on the carpeted stairs, her hand resting on the brass rail.

camera.movement: Handheld, low breath sway. Starts in the extreme close-up and eases slowly and steadily back and up, always in front of the knee, never orbiting, arriving exactly on the last frame.
camera.framing: From the first frame's extreme close-up to the last frame's framing.

motion: She steps down one stair: the knee bends a little as it takes her weight and her other foot lowers to the next tread; as the camera eases back, her hand resting on the rail comes into view. The strap stays seated on the knee every frame, the band pressing a shallow dent into the flesh. Everything in frame keeps its exact form, proportion and count from first frame to last — nothing melts, merges, splits, grows or becomes something else. The rigid shell never bends, flexes or stretches from any angle. Mass and momentum in all movement: heavy starts and settles slow, nothing at uniform speed; hands arrive last; fabric and straps lag and settle; objects drag with friction, never glide.
lighting: Capture characteristics exactly as in the first frame — same tone-mapping, noise and colour temperature, no grading change.
